name: Dorian Yates HIT
about: 2 on, 1 off, 2 on, 1 off. One working set to failure per exercise after feeder sets, rest-pause where marked.

ex.t: Primary clavicular builder. 1 set to failure + rest-pause (15 s).

Lengthened stretch. Strict failure, no rest-pause.

Long-head stretch, supinated grip. Strict failure.

Neutral grip, 1 s peak hold. Strict failure.

Vertical pull, supinated grip. Rest-pause 15 s.
Elbows out 45-60 degrees, pull to mid-lower sternum, no torso sway. Strict failure.
Elbow tucked to ribs, sweep to hip crease. Strict failure, no rest-pause.
Eye-level pulleys, horizontal arc. Rest-pause 10-15 s.

name: Push pull legs
about: 6 days on, 1 off, rotating: each muscle twice a week. Two versions of each day (A and B). Add weight when you hit the top of the rep range on every set.

name: PHUL
about: Power Hypertrophy Upper Lower: 4 days a week (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri). Heavy power days, then volume hypertrophy days.

name: PHAT
about: Power Hypertrophy Adaptive Training: 5 days a week. Two power days (Mon, Tue), then three hypertrophy days (Thu to Sat). Speed sets: 6 x 3 at about 65 to 70% of your power-day weight, moved fast.

name: Upper lower
about: 4 days a week (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri): each muscle twice a week, a heavier and a lighter version of each day.

name: Full body 3 days
about: Mon, Wed and Fri, a different full-body session each day. A good start for beginners or a busy week.

name: 5x5 strength
about: Workout A, rest, workout B, rest, rotating (about 3 sessions a week). 5 sets of 5 with the same weight; add 5 lb (2.5 kg) next time you complete all sets.

name: Novice linear A/B
about: 3 days a week (Mon, Wed, Fri), alternating workouts A and B. Few lifts, small jumps every session: the fastest way for a new lifter to get strong.

ex.t: Add 5 lb (2.5 kg) each session while you can.
Or power clean 5 x 3 if you know the lift.
Add 5 lb (2.5 kg) each session while you can.

name: GZCLP
about: 4 workouts in rotation, about 4 a week. Three tiers: T1 heavy (5 x 3), T2 moderate (3 x 10), T3 light pump work (3 x 15, last set as many reps as possible). When a T1 stalls, move to 6 x 2, then 10 x 1.

ex.t: T1. Last set: as many reps as possible.
T3. Last set: as many reps as possible.
T1. Last set: as many reps as possible.
T1. Last set: as many reps as possible.
T1. Last set: as many reps as possible.

name: 5/3/1 Boring But Big
about: 4 days a week (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri), one main lift a day. Week 1: 3 x 5, week 2: 3 x 3, week 3: 5/3/1, week 4: deload, using percentages of a training max (90% of your 1RM). Then 5 x 10 of the same lift at 50 to 60%.

ex.t: Main sets: 65/75/85% wk1, 70/80/90% wk2, 75/85/95% wk3. Last set: as many reps as possible.
Boring But Big: 50 to 60% of training max.
Main sets, as for press. Last set: as many reps as possible.
Main sets. Last set: as many reps as possible.
Main sets. Last set: as many reps as possible.

name: Texas Method
about: 3 days a week: volume on Monday (5 x 5 at about 90% of Friday's weight), a light recovery day Wednesday, and a new 5-rep best on Friday. For lifters who have run out of session-to-session progress.

ex.t: Work up to a new 5-rep best.

name: Arnold split
about: Chest and back, shoulders and arms, legs: each twice in 6 days, then a rest day. High volume, classic golden-era bodybuilding.

name: Bro split 5 days
about: One muscle group a day, Monday to Friday, weekends off. Lots of volume per session; each muscle trained once a week.

name: Heavy Duty HIT
about: Mike Mentzer style: very brief, very hard. One all-out set per exercise, pre-exhaust pairs done back to back, then 3 or more rest days. Add rest days when you stop getting stronger.

ex.t: Pre-exhaust: go straight to the next exercise.

name: Push pull legs 3 days
about: Push Monday, pull Wednesday, legs Friday: the classic split on 3 days a week. Each muscle once a week with enough volume to grow.

name: Powerbuilding 4 days
about: Each day starts with a heavy compound for strength (3 to 5 reps), then hypertrophy work (8 to 15 reps). Get stronger and bigger together.

name: Minimalist 2 days
about: Two full-body sessions a week (Mon and Thu), about 45 minutes each. Enough to build and keep strength when time is short.

name: Dumbbells at home
about: 3 full-body days a week (Mon, Wed, Fri) with just a pair of dumbbells and a bench or floor. Use a weight you can lift for the top of the range with 1 to 2 reps left.

ex.t: Per leg. Back foot on a bench if you have one.

name: Bodyweight basics
about: No equipment except a pull-up bar. 3 days a week (Mon, Wed, Fri). When you hit the top of a range on every set, move to a harder version (decline push-up, archer push-up, pistol progressions).

ex.t: Use a band or negatives if needed.
